hook_text: A charge can shove something it never touches. No rope, no contact — just refusal. Here is the machinery.
clip_script: Push two like charges together and something pushes back — with no rope, no touch, nothing visible. What is doing the pushing? Every charge travels with an invisible cushion of influence, filling the space around it: dense up close, thinning with distance, never quite ending. That cushion is the electric field. A second charge never deals with the faraway first one — it feels the cushion right where it stands. To map a cushion, physicists carry a candle: a small positive test charge. Wherever it gets shoved, draw an arrow. Away from positives. Toward negatives. Crowded arrows, strong field. And how strong is a spot? Do not quote the shove — a big visitor feels a big shove, a small one a small shove. Quote the shove PER COULOMB, like rand per litre at the shops. Five thousand newtons per coulomb is the price of standing there. One last twist: electrons read the whole map backwards — shoved against the arrows, every time. The field: every charge broadcasting into space, every point in space totalling what it receives.
visual_style: A dark space with a glowing charge wrapped in a soft radial cushion that fades outward; a tiny candle-like probe drifting spot to spot leaving arrows behind; a price-tag overlay reading newtons per coulomb; an electron sliding against the arrow flow.
mood: Quietly mind-bending — an invisible layer of reality made drawable.
pacing: Mysterious open, calm map-building middle, crisp backwards-electron twist at the end.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and learn to price any point in space.
